clue.text: Pull up if one is surrounded by a mass of people

indicators.note: the one is ringed by the crowd, so its letter goes inside the crowd's word

parts.note: a host is a great crowd or multitude
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A rescuer hauls someone up out of a dense crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist something is to raise it by rope or tackle, i.e. to haul it upwards.

clue.text: Bloomer results from adding German wine to winter berries

parts.note: holly bears its red berries in winter, at Christmas
hock is a white Rhine wine from Germany

explanation.surface: A recipe in which Rhine wine poured over Christmas berries yields a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder or a loaf; here it is simply a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall garden plant with large flowers is a bloomer, a thing that blooms.

clue.text: On his head is where coals of fire should be heaped

definitions.text: On his head is where coals of fire should be heaped

parts.words: On his head is where coals of fire should be heaped
parts.note: the Bible says kindness to an enemy heaps coals of fire on his head; read as two words, the coals belong in the fireplace

explanation.surface: A biblical saying about returning good for evil to an ungrateful man.
explanation.walkthrough: Romans 12:20: repaying an ungrateful person with kindness 'heaps coals of fire on his head'. Split the word as IN GRATE and coals of fire are just where they should be.
explanation.definitionFit: The ungrateful recipient of kindness is the person on whose head the biblical coals are heaped.

clue.text: A London rival of the Louvre upsets the French state

definitions.text: A London rival of the Louvre

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns the word over, so it is read bottom to top

parts.note: etat is the French word for state; the English 'state' also contains these letters, a coincidence that is not the wordplay

explanation.surface: A London museum outdoes the Paris one and annoys the French nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a London art gallery, set against the Louvre in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tate galleries in London compete with the Paris Louvre as a great art collection.

clue.text: Bread and fruit juice or sandwiches, pies, chips etc?

definitions.meaning: a meagre diet of the kind taken while fasting
quick takeaway meals served over the counter

explanation.definitionFit: Plain meals eaten during a period of abstinence, and also quick takeaway snacks such as burgers and chips.

clue.text: The Sugar Plum Fairy and all sorts of such lovely tunes?

definitions.text: The Sugar Plum Fairy and all sorts of such lovely tunes?

parts.words: The Sugar Plum Fairy and all sorts of such lovely tunes?
parts.note: the Nutcracker's Sugar Plum dance and liquorice allsorts both suggest confectionery, so lovely tunes named after them would be sugary ones

explanation.surface: A music critic praises the Nutcracker's Sugar Plum Fairy and other charming pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Liquorice allsorts are a British mixed sweet, and a sugar plum is a sweet too, so 'all sorts' carries a confectionery sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovely tunes are pleasing airs, sugary ones in the clue's confectionery picture.

clue.text: Yet a convicted miscreant might think it a bit thick

definitions.text: Yet a convicted miscreant might think it a bit thick

parts.words: Yet a convicted miscreant might think it a bit thick
parts.note: the word means slender, the opposite of thick, yet a money penalty may strike the offender as 'a bit thick', i.e. unfair

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer grumbles that the court's sentence was rather unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit thick' is British slang for unreasonable; the answer also means thin, so the convicted person finds the thin thing thick.
explanation.definitionFit: A monetary penalty imposed by a court is what the convicted offender resents as excessive.

clue.text: Given a directorship-after flotation?

definitions.meaning: appointed to a company's ruling body
aboard a vessel once it is afloat, or a company once it is floated on the market

explanation.definitionFit: A new director joins a company's ruling body; a passenger is aboard a ship once launched.

clue.text: Very much inclined to soak

definitions.meaning: sharply sloping, like a sheer hill
to leave something immersed in liquid

explanation.definitionFit: A sheer slope is sharply angled; to immerse something in liquid is to soak it.

clue.text: Have a fag and recover from a fagged out expression

definitions.meaning: a fag is British slang for a cigarette, so this means start smoking one

definitions.text: recover from a fagged out expression
definitions.meaning: a weary face that brightens

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fag' is British slang for a cigarette and 'fagged out' means exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite a cigarette, and for a tired face to brighten with animation.

clue.text: Its purpose is to run off-to Wapping or the Isle of Dogs maybe

definitions.text: Its purpose is to run off-to Wapping or the Isle of Dogs maybe

parts.words: Its purpose is to run off-to Wapping or the Isle of Dogs maybe
parts.note: run off means produce copies, not flee; Wapping and the Isle of Dogs are east London districts where newspapers moved their machines in the 1980s

explanation.surface: Someone eager to escape to the East End of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street papers moved their production to Wapping and the Isle of Dogs in London's Docklands, and 'run off' means print copies.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper production machinery exists to run off copies, and was relocated to those Docklands sites.

clue.text: Broken bone Len has to raise

indicators.note: a broken thing is in pieces, so these letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: Len has a fracture that needs lifting and setting.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to the peerage is to make them a noble.

clue.text: Truly a king for only twelve months

parts.note: yea is an old word for indeed or truly
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone was really only monarch for a single year.
explanation.definitionFit: A calendar period of twelve months is a year.

clue.text: Little Catherine Pool!

definitions.meaning: a pet form of the name Catherine
a shared fund of money, as in a card game

explanation.definitionFit: A familiar form of the name Catherine, and a common fund of stakes in a game.

clue.text: Flirt with improvising on a guitar?

definitions.meaning: a seductive woman who flirts
to play a simple improvised accompaniment

explanation.definitionFit: A seductress, and to extemporise a simple backing on an instrument.

clue.text: It sounds like a personal claim for time

indicators.note: the clue says the word is only heard like the claim, so the written form differs

parts.note: saying 'that's ours' stakes a claim of possession

explanation.surface: A worker's request for time off sounds like personal pleading.
explanation.walkthrough: With a silent H the answer is said like OURS.
explanation.definitionFit: Periods of sixty minutes measure time.

clue.text: To physicians they must mean final failure

definitions.text: To physicians they must mean final failure

parts.words: To physicians they must mean final failure
parts.note: a doctor's patient who ends up buried represents the doctor's ultimate failure

explanation.surface: A grim thought about what doctors regard as their ultimate defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Burial vaults hold the dead, the patients a doctor could not save.

clue.text: Hiking enthusiast to be avoided by one who drinks and drives

definitions.meaning: someone who loves the open highway, read literally

definitions.text: to be avoided by one who drinks and drives
definitions.meaning: a final drink before leaving a pub

explanation.definitionFit: A last drink before departing, read literally as someone keen on walking the highway.

clue.text: What the faint-hearted Sandhurst cadet did on final parade

definitions.text: What the faint-hearted Sandhurst cadet did on final parade

parts.words: What the faint-hearted Sandhurst cadet did on final parade
parts.note: a cadet graduating completes training at the final parade; a timid one might also faint

explanation.surface: A nervous army officer cadet collapses at his graduation ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandhurst is the British Army's officer academy; cadets graduate at a passing-out parade, and to faint is also to lose consciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: Both graduating from military training and fainting are described by the same phrase.

clue.text: If strands go be prepared for them to scatter on the floor

definitions.text: If strands go be prepared for them to scatter on the floor

indicators.note: scattering spreads things in disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that if the threads snap, beads will roll across the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to scatter' rearranges IF STRANDS GO BE, and the whole clue describes what happens when a necklace breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklace of threaded pearls or baubles spills them over the floor when its thread snaps.

clue.text: So top artist gets no top part in the chorus

parts.note: PRA is the President of the Royal Academy, the leading British artist

explanation.surface: A star painter is refused the leading vocal role in the choir.
explanation.walkthrough: PRA (President of the Royal Academy) is a crossword convention for a top artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest voice in a choir is the treble line sung by women or boys.

clue.text: Fan called for by a doctor going around a swamp

indicators.note: the doctor's letters circle the swamp, so the swamp sits inside them

parts.note: mire is boggy ground

explanation.surface: A fan summons a doctor who is wading round a bog.
explanation.definitionFit: An enthusiastic follower or fan is someone who looks up to another.

clue.text: Bill gets a cloak

definitions.meaning: a bill is a narrow headland, as in Portland Bill
a sleeveless garment worn round the shoulders

explanation.walkthrough: Portland Bill is a headland on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A promontory such as Portland Bill, and a sleeveless shoulder garment.

clue.text: The winner at boxing in a picnic hamper

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words picnic hamper, straddling the space

explanation.surface: A boxing victor celebrates with a picnic basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion is the title-holding winner of a contest.

clue.text: Health resort in Mediterranean country

parts.note: a spa is a resort with mineral springs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A holiday at a wellness resort on the Med.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iberian nation with a long Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: See about a thousand duck

indicators.note: the first word goes round the second, so the thousand sits inside

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Look at a flock of a thousand ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: A smee is an old name for a duck such as the smew or wigeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional name for certain wild waterfowl such as the wigeon.

clue.text: Rent is pronouncedly higher

indicators.note: the word is said like the other one, though spelt differently

parts.note: taken as written: it is the word said aloud

explanation.surface: A complaint that the rent has clearly gone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To rent something, a car say, is to take it on hire.

clue.text: Field marshal who carried little weight?

definitions.meaning: William ..., British field marshal of the Burma campaign
someone thin, not heavy

explanation.definitionFit: Viscount William Slim commanded in Burma; a thin person is light in build.

clue.text: Man needs sex appeal in a woman

indicators.note: the sex appeal is placed inside the woman's word

parts.note: a dame is a woman
it is an old word for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A man looks for allure in a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' for sex appeal comes from the 1920s 'It girl'. An Adamite is a descendant of Adam.
explanation.definitionFit: A descendant of Adam is a human being.

clue.text: Learn lay out in so famous an Italian city

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the short word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: laying out arranges things differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lessons on setting out a famous Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'famous an' is part of the surface only; Salerno, south of Naples, is the Italian city meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A port south of Naples on the Tyrrhenian coast, scene of the 1943 Allied landings.

clue.text: Computer centre for a production-line worker

definitions.meaning: the central unit that executes a computer's instructions
someone who treats or packages goods

explanation.definitionFit: A computer's central unit carries out instructions; a factory hand treats raw goods.

clue.text: To a degree a deserter became a French revolutionary

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a university degree
a rat is one who deserts, like rats leaving a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A graduate turns traitor and joins the revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Paul Marat was a radical of the French Revolution, killed in his bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Marat was a radical journalist of the 1789 uprising in France.
